body.x: Marking its third edition this year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea’s benchmark future industry exhibition, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the expo establishes a new milestone for global industry by organically linking core technologies across four key advanced sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Encompassing the achievements of Daegu Metropolitan City’s forward-looking industrial cultivation, leading domestic and international tech enterprises alongside promising startups will assemble to unveil next-generation, field-validated technologies poised to transform everyday life and industrial operations. Concurrently featuring international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation initiatives, the event is set to serve as a pivotal exchange hub leading technological collaboration and innovation far beyond Asia.

Participating as an official Global Media Award partner for FIX 2026, VietnamPlus is the official digital general news portal under the Vietnam News Agency (VNA), Vietnam’s state-run news agency. Recording approximately 30 million monthly page views—the highest among VNA’s digital media subsidiaries—the outlet commands extensive social media influence, engaging younger demographics with 700,000 YouTube subscribers and over 1 million TikTok followers. Transmitting news in five languages—Vietnamese, English, French, Chinese, and Russian—VietnamPlus functions as a vital bridge connecting Vietnam’s domestic business ecosystem with international markets. Recognized for its journalistic credibility through accolades such as the World Association of News Publishers (WAN-IFRA) International Digital Journalism Award, VietnamPlus returns to Daegu two years after covering FIX 2024 to introduce promising South Korean technology companies and breakthroughs to the Vietnamese market amid its nationwide digital transformation and smart manufacturing upgrades. An advance interview was conducted with Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and Deputy Editor-in-Chief of VietnamPlus, to discuss cross-border technological cooperation and his expectations for FIX 2026.

body.x: Q1. Could you introduce your media outlet to Korean readers and highlight your key competitive strengths?
VietnamPlus is the official e-newspaper of the Vietnam News Agency (VNA), the country’s state news provider.

VietnamPlus is a general news outlet, but we have always paid close attention to technology, innovation, and emerging trends. Over the years, we have covered major developments in digital transformation, artificial intelligence, new technologies, startups, and the digital economy, both in Vietnam and on the international stage.
VietnamPlus is a relatively small newsroom, but we have achieved a significant reach. We have the highest monthly readership among VNA’s digital publications, with around 30 million views.

Our reach also extends across social media platforms. The VietnamPlus YouTube channel has more than 700,000 subscribers, while our TikTok channel has more than 1 million followers. Our official Facebook pages also have tens of thousands of followers. These platforms allow us to reach different audiences, especially younger readers who increasingly consume news on social media and other digital platforms.

Another strength of VietnamPlus is our multilingual platform. We publish in Vietnamese, English, French, Chinese and Russian, allowing stories about Vietnamese and international businesses to reach audiences beyond Vietnam.

VietnamPlus has received various national and international journalism awards, including Vietnam’s National Press Award and international digital journalism awards from World Association of News Publishers (WAN-IFRA). Thanks to our reputation and reach, we have worked with major domestic brands and corporations such as Vietnam Airlines, Vietjet Air, Vinamilk, TH true MILK, VNG, Vingroup, Sun Group and Nestlé Vietnam.

We see ourselves as a bridge between the business community and our readers. In addition to covering established corporations, VietnamPlus regularly introduces innovative startups and emerging businesses, helping them communicate their products, ideas and new business models to a wider audience. We are particularly interested in companies that use technology to create new solutions or to address social and economic challenges.
We hope our participation in FIX 2026 will help us discover new stories and connect our Vietnamese audience with the latest technology and innovation trends from Korea.
Q2. What are your perspectives on current trends across industrial technology, mobility, and AI?

In industrial technology, I see a major shift in Vietnam from adopting digital tools to building smarter, more automated production systems. Vietnamese manufacturers are interested in smart factories, industrial robots, machine vision, IoT, digital twins, and AI-powered quality control. Also, AI is used to perform tasks such as analyzing data, monitoring machines, and predicting equipment failures.

This trend is closely connected to Vietnam’s ambition to strengthen its position in electronics, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and supporting industries. In 2026, the Vietnamese government identified strategic technologies such as digital technologies, robotics and automation, semiconductor technology, and advanced energy and materials as priority areas for development. It has also prioritized technologies including digital twins, advanced robots, autonomous equipment, and autonomous vehicles. Mobility is another area where we can see a visible transformation. Vietnam is experiencing rapid growth in electric vehicles, particularly electric cars and bikes. According to an International Energy Agency report, electric car sales in Vietnam more than doubled in 2025, with electric vehicles accounting for nearly 40% of new car sales. This makes Vietnam one of the most dynamic electric vehicle markets in Southeast Asia.

I think the mobility story in Vietnam is becoming broader than replacing gasoline vehicles with electric ones. We begin to see an ecosystem that combines electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, digital platforms, and technology-enabled transportation services. The development of electric taxi and ride-hailing fleets (as with GreenSM in Vietnam) is one example.

For me, the most interesting aspect is the convergence of AI, industrial technology, and mobility. AI makes factories smarter, robots more capable, and vehicles more intelligent while data and connectivity link these technologies into larger ecosystems. I believe this convergence will be one of the most important technology trends to watch in Vietnam and the world in the coming years.

body.x: Q3. What key issues and topics related to FIX 2026 will interest your readership most?

As the Vietnamese government is pushing for innovation and digital transformation, our audience is more interested in technologies that can have a practical impact on the economy and everyday life. For FIX 2026, we are focused on robotics, AI and smart technologies that can improve productivity, address work challenges and enhance quality of life.

For example, we would like to learn more about how robots and AI are being used in manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, education and other sectors. We are really interested in technologies that have moved beyond the demonstration stage and are already being applied in real-world environments.

Another topic of interest is how AI and robotics may change the relationship between people and machines. As Vietnam’s economy becomes more digital and its industries seek higher productivity, we believe our readers will want to understand which jobs and tasks can be supported or transformed by AI and robots, what new skills workers will need, and how businesses can prepare for this transition.

We would also like to explore the Korean experience. Korea is one of the world’s leading technology and manufacturing economies, so FIX 2026 provides an opportunity to see how Korean companies are applying AI, robotics, smart manufacturing, and mobility technologies in practice.
We want to discover solutions relevant to Vietnam and identify Korean startups and technology companies with potential for cooperation or expansion into the Vietnamese market.
Q4. How was your experience during FIX 2024, and what are your expectations for this year’s exhibition?

The first FIX event attended by a VietnamPlus representative in 2024 left a strong impression on us, particularly in terms of how far Korea has progressed in automation, robotics, and future mobility. 2 years have passed since then, and the global technology landscape has changed significantly, especially with the rapid development of artificial intelligence. So, one of our main expectations for FIX 2026 is to see how AI is being integrated with robotics, mobility, manufacturing, and other smart technologies.

I also expect FIX 2026 to show us more examples of technologies that have moved from the laboratory or demonstration stage into practical use. Korean companies are known for their ability to identify emerging technologies, experiment with them, and turn them into products and services for everyday life.

This makes Korea particularly interesting for us as journalists from Vietnam, where businesses and policymakers are also looking for practical ways to use AI and automation to improve productivity and competitiveness.

We also want to discover what has changed since our previous visit. Which technologies that were emerging or experimental in 2024 have now become commercially viable? How are Korean companies combining AI with robotics, smart manufacturing, and mobility to create new products and business models?
We want to bring back stories that can help our Vietnamese audience understand where technology is heading and what Vietnam can learn from Korea’s experience.

body.x: Q5. How do you evaluate the FIX Innovation Awards press conference featuring presentations from past award recipients and Best of FIX companies?

As someone working in the media industry, I find the FIX Innovation Awards press conference important because it can serve as a launchpad for innovative Korean startups and technology companies to gain visibility among the public, potential partners, and international markets.

I appreciate the fact that the event brings together international media. The presence of global news organizations means that the stories emerging from FIX do not have to remain within Korea. Journalists can discover promising companies on-site and introduce their technologies, products, and ideas to audiences in their home countries. So, the press conference can help create a bridge between Korean innovation and the global technology market. For startups, this kind of exposure is valuable. Many young companies may have strong technologies and innovative ideas, but gaining visibility and building credibility outside their home market can be challenging.

From a journalist’s perspective, I also find the format useful because it is more than just a product demonstration. Through presentations and direct interaction with the companies, journalists can understand the technology, business model, target market, and each company’s development strategy. This gives us a more informed basis for evaluating which technologies have genuine potential and which stories may be relevant to audiences in our home countries.

I also think the combination of the on-site global media zone, live-streaming sessions, and the press conference is particularly effective. These elements extend the event’s reach beyond the exhibition venue and enable companies to communicate with audiences who cannot attend FIX in person. So, the organizers are not simply creating an awards ceremony but building an international media platform that can help promising local companies gain attention and take their first steps onto the global stage.

body.x: Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting from the front lines of technological developments by innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea’s high-tech landscape.
